subject: general
question: The light from a point source is rendered parallel by a concave mirror. What is the position of the light source ?

options.text: Between focus and centre of curvature

solution:
The correct answer is __**At Focus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• If an object is at infinity from a concave mirror, the parallel rays of light, after reflection converges at focus.
 
• Hence, the image formed is the focus of the mirror.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

__
 
• A concave mirror has a reflective surface that is curved inward and away from the light source.
 
• Concave mirrors reflect light inward to one focal point.
 
• The image formed by the concave lens when an object is placed at infinity is virtual, erect, highly diminished and at focus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Concave mirror: It is cut out of a reflective sphere is a spherical mirror. If the reflective surface is on the side curved inwards, it is a concave mirror.

 
 
• These mirrors are commonly used as shaving mirrors or by dentists and even in telescopes.
 
• The reflected image is magnified but the field of view is limited.
 
• these mirrors are also called as converging mirrors.
